_doc: Large batch L05 themed pass (TEMPLATE.md sections 9 and 10): lichen reindeer, red stag, gorse beast, the moss / lichen / peat / coral golems, emperor scorpion, giant bumblebee. New motifs live in motifs/large_L05.js (31, glyph/motion ids prefixed L05-, 4 custom chain effects: gorse fuse, rut bellow, bog steam, bumblebee flight). Every piece (unique, class and x0) has a hand note. All 9 signature motifs are used by no other creature; lichen-rosette (the lichen golem's crust) is lent to the lichen reindeer for its lichen cloak and moss mantle. The Sonnet family overrides in overrides/large/L05.json stay the Generic fallback; the repeats it left (golem mend x2/x3, coral and peat thorn x2, stag slash x2) are split here by motif or layout, and its seven review flags are answered by the pictures: Gorse Flare = flowers flaring like flame, Bog Fist = a peat fist out of the bog, Rut Call = a roar, Pollen Puff = pollen baskets puffing, Anemone Sting = anemone tentacles, Autumn Rut = a royal rack clash, Lichen Antler Sweep = a lichen-crusted rack.

lichen-reindeer.notes: Lichen reindeer of the tundra and mountains: a grey-fawn reindeer whose long rack is crusted with grey-green lichen, a brow shovel over the muzzle, a pale neck ruff; it paws craters in the snow to reach the lichen it lives on, the herd wheels in a circle when pressed, and it holds a grudge. It steps up like a herd on the march.

u0.n: Antler Sweep: the lichen-crusted rack swings off the edge left then right, flakes of crust flying

u1.n: Herd Wheel: reindeer trot out in a circle round the piece and back, snow kicked up behind them

u2.n: Snow Dig: hooves paw craters in the snow crust and green-grey lichen sprigs rise out of them

u3.n: Lichen Cloak: lichen rosettes push out of the hide and spread ring by ring, crusty and bristling

b0.n: Cloven Hoof: a cloven hoof kicks off the edge, the snow crust bursting

b1.n: Lichen Antler Sweep: the crusted rack sweeps the length of the edge in one swing

b2.n: Moss Mantle: a mantle of lichen and moss rosettes lies along the edge, slowly growing

b3.n: Tundra Nudge: a rack nudges out and drops back, snow sliding off it

x0.n: Antler Lunge: the rack lunges off the edge with grudge marks popping

red-stag.notes: Red stag of forest and mountain in the autumn rut: a red-brown coat, a shaggy neck, a wide royal rack with crowned tops; it bellows with breath steaming, clashes antlers and hides in golden bracken. It lands heavy, and the bellow (croak arcs) is its sound.

u0.n: Autumn Rut: the royal rack is lowered, tossed and clashed off the edge in a white star

u1.n: Tine Hook: the rack drives the length of the edge, the brow tines hooking the foe

u2.n: Bracken Dodge: golden bracken croziers unroll out of the edge and the stag melts in and back out of them

u3.n: Rut Call: bellowing stags at spots round the edge, roar arcs tying them together, the roar rolling on to the next piece

b0.n: Rut Antler Swing: the rack swings out and crashes back in a puff of dust

b1.n: Rut Snort: the stag snorts off the edge, breath steaming

b2.n: Rut Hide: bracken fronds bristle up out of the edge and hide the red hide

b3.n: Rut Forage: fronds unroll and rise off the edge, seed and spore dust drifting

x0.n: Red Rut Charge: stags charge off the edge head-down, turf flying from the clash

gorse-beast.notes: Gorse beast of grassland and forest: a shaggy heap of dense green spines covered in yellow pea flowers that smell of coconut and hum with bees; gorse burns hot and its seed pods crack open in the sun. It trundles in slow and heavy.

u0.n: Gorse Flare: gorse sprigs slam out and their yellow flowers flare up like flame, char and spit seed sparks, and the flare runs on along the edge like a fuse

u1.n: Sun Soak: pea flowers open in the sun and rise off the edge, rays glinting

u2.n: Golden Bloom: a row of golden flowers opens along the edge, pollen drifting, bees landing

u3.n: Prickly Hug: dense spiny clumps bristle out of the edge, yellow flowers tucked between the spines

b0.n: Gorse Whip: a spiny clump lashes off the edge

b1.n: Bloom Cloud: flowers burst off the edge in a cloud of pollen

b2.n: Spiky Thicket: a thicket of spines stands along the edge

b3.n: Sunbathe Mend: flowers open to the sun and rise, a bee landing

x0.n: Shaggy Heap Crash: the spiny heap crashes out and back, clods flying

moss-golem.notes: Moss golem of forest, rainforest and mountain: a body of grey stones under a thick green moss cushion, spore stalks with brown capsules nodding on top; it punches with boulder fists and grows its moss back. It heaves up out of the forest floor.

u0.n: Boulder Fist: mossy stone fists wind up and punch off the edge, cracks flashing, moss shaken loose

u1.n: Moss Cloak: a thick moss mat hangs along the edge, spore capsules nodding

u2.n: Regrow: moss cushions grow back and rise, spore stalks shooting up, a capsule popping

u3.n: Shed Pebble: a mossy stone shrugs out and drops back, clods of moss falling

b0.n: Moss Creeper Whip: a creeper of moss lashes off the edge

b1.n: Mossy Spore Burst: spore stalks burst off the edge, a fall of spores

b2.n: Mossy Mantle: the moss mat bristles out, capsules on end

b3.n: Sap Patch-Up: moss cushions rise beaded with sap and dew

x0.n: Rockfall Slam: mossy boulders drop off the edge and fall

lichen-golem.notes: Lichen golem of the mountains: a small body of loose scree held together by a flaky grey-green lichen crust, pixie-cup lichens drinking the rain; it tumbles like scree and sheds sharp crusted flakes. It rolls in like a falling stone.

u0.n: Scree Tumble: lichen-spotted scree slabs slam out end over end and fall back

u1.n: Lichen Mend: lichen rosettes rise off the edge, spreading ring by ring

u2.n: Rain Soak: pixie-cup lichens catch rain drops, fill to the brim and rise

u3.n: Flake Chunk: a sharp crusted flake flips point first along the edge

b0.n: Lichen Tendril: grey-green tendrils lash out, a crust flake at each tip

b1.n: Grey Dust Puff: scree chips burst out of the edge in grey dust and settle back

b2.n: Grey Lichen Cloak: lichen rosettes push out of the scree and bristle

b3.n: Rain-Drink Refill: cups fill and rain beads run along the crust

x0.n: Scree Tumble Slam: a scree slab tumbles the length of the edge

peat-golem.notes: Peat golem of the wetlands: a dark brown body of cut peat turves full of root threads, a hair of reeds with brown seed heads, steam breathing out of its cracks; it heaves wet fists out of the bog and slumps into a wall. It arrives slow and wet.

u0.n: Peat Slump: stacked peat turves hold along the edge, the top turves slumping and settling

u1.n: Bog Fist: wet peat fists heave up out of bog pools and claw at the foe, mud splatting

u2.n: Reed Bristle: the reed hair bristles out, brown seed heads swaying

u3.n: Steam Vent: steam curls up out of cracks in the peat, and a bank of steam drifts on to the next piece

b0.n: Reed Whip: reeds lash off the edge

b1.n: Peat Dust Cloud: turves crumble out of the edge in brown dust and settle back

b2.n: Packed Peat Wall: packed turves push out of the edge and hold

b3.n: Bog Refill: bog water wells up, bubbles rising, the peat fist lifting with it

x0.n: Stack Collapse: the turf stack topples off the edge and falls

coral-golem.notes: Coral golem of coast and island: a plated body of branching pink coral with white polyps, sea anemones swaying in its cracks and barnacles welded to its armour; it bobs up like something lifted by the tide.

u0.n: Spiny Branch: branching coral bristles out of the edge, polyps opening at every tip

u1.n: Anemone Sway: anemones sway out of the edge in the swell and draw back

u2.n: Anemone Sting: anemone tentacles drop off the edge trailing sting lines

u3.n: Stack Lock: barnacle cones lock along the edge, lids snapping shut

b0.n: Sharp Branch Whip: a coral branch lashes off the edge

b1.n: Coral Anemone Sting: tentacles lash out, a white sting flash at the tips

b2.n: Polyp Plating: barnacle plates push out, cirri combing

b3.n: Low-Tide Mend: barnacles open in the returning tide and rise, bubbles going up

x0.n: Stack Crumble: coral branches break off the edge and fall

emperor-scorpion.notes: Emperor scorpion of desert and rainforest: huge, glossy black, with thick knobbly claws and a curled tail; under moonlight its armour glows pale blue-green, so every glyph is black with a glowing outline. Shy, it scuttles sideways, and many of them crowd together.

u0.n: Pincer Clamp: thick black claws open wide, slam out and snap shut in a star

u1.n: Stinger Arch: glowing tails arch over and pale venom beads drop off the stings

u2.n: Plate Fold: glossy plates fold over each other and push out like shingles, a glint sliding across

u3.n: Shy Scuttle: glowing scorpions scuttle sideways out of the edge and back

b0.n: Pincer Pinch: claws lunge off the edge and pinch

b1.n: Stinger Thrust: the tail drives the length of the edge, sting first

b2.n: Emperor Glossy Carapace: glossy plates hold along the edge, glints sliding over them

b3.n: Emperor Shy Scuttle: glowing scorpions blink from spot to spot

x0.n: Armoured Ram: the armour rams out and back, dust flying

giant-bumblebee.notes: Giant bumblebee of grassland and forest: a huge round furry bee with a yellow band, a black band and a white tail, wings far too small for it, orange pollen baskets on its legs; it bumbles about and bumps into things. It hovers before it settles.

u0.n: Bumble Bump: big furry bees wobble off the edge and squash flat on the foe, and one bumbles on to the next piece

u1.n: Fuzz Coat: the thick banded fuzz stands up along the edge, pollen clinging

u2.n: Pollen Puff: pollen baskets puff orange clouds at spots round the edge, tied by drifting grains

u3.n: Honey Sting: barbed stings drip amber honey beads that fall off the edge

b0.n: Fuzzy Nibble: a bee bumbles out to nibble, pollen shaken off

b1.n: Barb Jab: a barbed sting jabs the length of the edge

b2.n: Velvet Armour: the fuzz lies smooth as velvet, a sheen running over it

b3.n: Drone Dart: drones dart from spot to spot

x0.n: Buzzing Bulk: a huge bee body-slams out and back in a puff of pollen
